gaps.title: Party order cannot be changed from the main menu
gaps.detail: FIX LIVES IN src/ui/menu.js (P13), so P18 may not touch it. P18 exposes the whole thing ready to call: Party.wagonMenu() opens the roster window, and Party.reorder, Party.swap, Party.move and Party.canRemove are the operations behind it. Today the only way in is talking to the wagon on the field or calling __DQ.wagonMenu(). The main menu needs a Party entry that calls Party.wagonMenu(), or its own screen built on those four functions.

events.note: Opened the main menu in demos/P17.html with 4 walking, 5 riding: m-cmd items are Talk, Items, Spells, Equip, Status, Tactics, Search, Misc. No Party and no Wagon entry, and Misc does not lead to one (menuPath stays at command). In /index.html the party plugin is not installed at all, so __DQ.wagonMenu does not exist either. The only door to the roster is walking up to the wagon prop on the field, which in the real game does not exist.

gaps.title: Roster window loses your place on every keypress and refuses in silence
gaps.detail: Measured in demos/P17.html with 4 walking and 5 riding. Party.wagonMenu rebuilds UI.menu inside its for(;;) loop with no initial:, so every selection destroys and recreates the window and the cursor snaps back to row 1. Recorded sequence: cursor on Bram, press Z (he is the leader and cannot be moved) — a buzzer plays, NO message appears, title stays Who walks, who rides?, and selectedLabel is back to Bram. Then ArrowDown, Z on Halvard the guest — same silent buzzer, selectedLabel reads Bram again. Three further presses of ArrowDown and Enter produced no swap at all: party stayed Bram, Halvard, Bobble, Dollop II. A six-year-old pressing the confirm button is told nothing and loses their place, which breaks CANON rule 4 (every why can-t I gets one sentence) and CLARITY. party.js already HAS the sentences — Party.move returns Halvard travels with you his own way and Bram leads the way, he stays — and wagonMenu throws them away. Fix, all in src/world/party.js: keep one menu alive across the loop (or pass initial: the id last touched), show the refusal line in a message box or under the title when canRemove is false, and after a successful swap re-render the list and stay open instead of returning, so a child can rearrange three monsters in one visit. While there: the rows show only a name and Lv, so you choose who fights without seeing a single HP figure — add HP/MP to each row.
